evidence.result: exit 1 — 2 tests failed, both with AssertionError: expected '/brand/chat' to match /[?&](deal|creator)=/. After a successful deals.create or creators.invite the modal navigates to a bare /brand/chat carrying no identifier for the creator it just messaged

rows.subject: src/pages/brand-chat.tsx:926 — silent fallback to an arbitrary deal room

evidence.result: the live-mode effect computes match from ?deal= then ?creator=, then runs setSelectedDeal(match || liveDealRooms[0]). With neither param present match is undefined, so the brand is dropped into liveDealRooms[0] — a different creator's thread — and when liveDealRooms is still empty the effect returns at :920 and selectedDeal stays null, so no conversation opens at all

evidence.command: grep -n resolveCounterparty influora-api/.../DealService.java ; grep -n counterpartyId src/pages/brand-chat.tsx src/pages/brand-messages.tsx
evidence.result: DealService.resolveCounterparty returns collaboration.getCreatorId() and resolves the profile with creatorProfileRepository.findByUserId(...), so counterpartyId is a USER id. brand-chat.tsx:209 and brand-messages.tsx:274 both key their room list on that value, while every ?creator= producer passes a CreatorProfile id (api.ts:1551 states the contract). The two lookups compare different id spaces, so even the callers that DO pass ?creator= fall through to index 0

rows.subject: brand messaging entry points — three callers, two destinations

evidence.result: three entry points disagree: creator-discovery.tsx:536 goes to /brand/chat with no param, brand-campaign-detail.tsx:1224 goes to /brand/chat?creator=, brand-creator-profile.tsx:571 goes to /brand/messages?creator=. Two different message surfaces are registered in App.tsx (:235 /brand/chat, :259 /brand/messages) for the same user intent
